title: Out of memory (OOM) during window function on large data
body:
### What happens?

I'm getting an OOM error on a 1 billion row table stored in a DuckDB database using the below query on DuckDB 0.8.0. I'm trying to create a new column with values for each corresponding group specified by the window. For this work I only have access to a machine with about 10 GB of usable RAM for DuckDB (16 GB total) given the security requirements of the data. 

I do see that there are several GBs of temp files on disk being created while this query runs.

Below is the query that causes the error:

```
con.sql("""create or replace table new_table as SELECT 
    Pid, 
    Planid, 
    Claimid, 
    'CLAIM' || dense_rank() OVER(PARTITION BY Pid, Planid ORDER BY Claimid) AS Fake_Claimid
FROM big_table;""")

OutOfMemoryException: Out of Memory Error: failed to pin block of size 262KB (10.0GB/10.0GB used)
```

### To Reproduce

The data types are double, double, and varchar for Patid, Planid, and Claimid respectively.

Patid is fixed length of 15 - e.g. 123456789012345
Planid is fixed length of 15 - e.g. 123456789012345
Claimid is fixed length of 10 - e.g. ABC123ABC12

@participant2 Helped me out by posting a proposed data generator script (below) to give us a start with generating example data.

CREATE TABLE big_table AS
    SELECT 
        (i % 500)::DOUBLE AS "Patid",
        (i % 5000)::DOUBLE AS "Planid",
        uuid()::VARCHAR AS "Claimid",
    FROM range(1000000000) tbl(i);

I have also attached a Python-based faker script that gets pretty close as well, but it goes to Parquet as an intermediate step instead of direct within DuckDB. This code should produce about 10 million rows every ~90 seconds or so on a decent computer. 

`pip install -r requirements.txt`

```
# Generate fake data
import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
from faker import Faker
import random

# Create a Faker instance
fake = Faker()

# Define the total number of rows and row size of each chunk
num_rows = 1_000_000_000
chunk_size = 10_000_000

# Calculate the number of chunks
num_chunks = num_rows // chunk_size

# Cardinality is about 2% of all rows, so number of unique Pids and unique Planids is 2% of total rows
num_unique_values = int(num_rows * .02)  

# Generate unique Pid and Planids
start_number = 100000000000000
values = [_ for _ in range(start_number, start_number + num_unique_values)]

# Create a PyArrow Table schema
fields = [
    pa.field('Pid', pa.int64()),
    pa.field('Planid', pa.int64()),
    pa.field('Claimid', pa.string()),
]
schema = pa.schema(fields)

# Generate a chunk of data
for i in range(num_chunks):
    data = {
        'Pid': [random.choice(values) for _ in range(chunk_size)],
        'Planid': [random.choice(values) for _ in range(chunk_size)],
        'Claimid': [''.join(fake.random_letters(length=10)).upper() for _ in range(chunk_size)]
    }

    # Convert the chunk to a PyArrow Table
    table = pa.Table.from_pydict(data)

    # Write the chunk to a Parquet file
    pq.write_table(table, f'faker_data_output\\fake_data-{i}.parquet')
    print(f"Wrote chunk {i}")
```

[requirements.txt](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/files/11637989/requirements.txt)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@reporter After looking into this some more, the problem is that you are heavily resource constrained. The query has a large number of partitions, which we hash into at most 1024 hash groups. Even with the new paging, each thread will need to keep at a minimum `partitions * block size * overlap` bytes = 1024 * 262000 * 2 bytes ~= 500MB. If you run the query on a large number of threads (e.g., 16) , then it can exceed the memory limit (e.g., 8GB). So one option is to use `PRAGMA threads=4` or something to restrict the memory usage. You would also need to set up `PRAGMA temp_directory='...'` so the data can be paged.

I will submit the new out-of-core partitioning, which will at least allow you some control. After that, I will need to check the thread count and partitions to make sure that we don't exceed the memory budget.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> The data I am looking at is stored in multiple parquet files and has ~ 142 mio records, and the number of groups is of the same order of magnitude. (My use case is some kind of "update pipeline", where this particular query retrieves the latest update per actual ID; usually there are only a bunch of updates per ID, so the group size is usually <= 10). I use a duckdb-arrow combination to perform the query arrow to write the result back other parquet files.

It sounds like you are looking for the latest change in each group? If so, you probably want to use the `arg_max` aggregate instead of windowing:

```sql
SELECT group, arg_max(val, timestamp) AS val
FROM relation
GROUP BY ALL
```
